items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: He said, 'Oh I don't know, somewhere between Gil Evans and Claus Ogerman.'

ctx.x: Well I’m looking forward to hearing the Bobby Darin project.

It’s wonderful really. We were sitting down at lunch and Colomby’s looking at me and saying, “You know, I’m really thinking about this as extended arrangements.” I said, “Yeah?” He said, “Yeah, some like five, six, seven minutes.” I said, “Really? With a vocal?” He said, “Yeah. The vocal is only going to be just like an instrument.” I turned to Gary LeMel and said, “Really? You’re up for this?” He said, “Yeah, yeah, it’s great, love the idea.” So I said to Bobby Colomby, “Well sort of what parameters do you want…

opportunity to — and I got Elvin Jones and I got the Brecker Brothers and I got this wonderful cellist. So we went from “Easy Living,” which is Michael Brecker and myself and cello, we went from there all the way to “Mack the Knife” with a big band and going through all the lyrics of “Mack the Knife,” including the German lyrics, so there’s like ten choruses that start in Germany and then go through Dixieland and then go to modern swing band and then end up in Germany again. It’s very interesting.
